### Also covered by

Riehl, *Category Theory in Context*, 2nd ed., §3.1, printed pp. 90–91 (PDF pp. 110–111), item `riehl:3.1:def-direct-sums` — the unnumbered

"identity matrix" morphism from an `I`-indexed coproduct to the corresponding product (zero off the
diagonal, identity on it) is an isomorphism for finite `I`; the common value is the direct sum, and
morphisms between finite direct sums are matrices of components composed by matrix multiplication,
the `(i,k)` entry of a composite being the sum over `j` of `g_(j,k) ∘ f_(i,j)`. This is precisely the
n-ary canonical comparison and matrix calculus this issue already scopes.

(id △ zero_mor) ▽ (zero_mor △ id)`) with its four matrix entries at `:287-320`, `:227`
(`cartesian_biproduct`), `:101` (`bi_copair_pair : bi_copair B u v ∘ bi_pair B f g ≈ padd (u ∘ f) (v ∘ g)`,
the 2-entry instance of the sum formula), `:573` (`bicartesian_preadditive`), `Structure/Biproduct.v:42`
(`Record Biproduct`), and the 2×2 interchange `Structure/Bicartesian.v:39` (`fork_merge`).
